item.title: After P2P pause, Nigeria’s Quidax turns to Lisk for regulated stablecoin rails
item.description: Builders on the Lisk network can now use Quidax’s digital asset infrastructure to access stablecoins and local currencies.

item.title: Fintechs may finally get regulatory clarity as Kenya’s Central Bank reviews laws
item.description: In a tender notice on Monday, the regulator has invited consultants to help review the two laws that define its powers in a bid to strengthen provisions related to digital banking, fintech regulation, consumer protection, and cybersecurity.”

item.title: Spiro raises $50 million to scale battery swapping network
item.description: Spiro has closed a $50 million debt funding backed by Afreximbank, Nithio, and Africa Go Green Fund, after a $100 million raise in October 2025.

item.title: We tested M-PESA’s latest feature Shiriki Pay. Here’s how it works.
item.description: Shiriki Pay, baked in the M-PESA app, allows a user to add up to two beneficiaries who can pay merchants using the sponsor’s wallet balance, subject to a preset monthly cap.

item.title: Why VaulFi is building a stablecoin-powered super app for North Africa
item.description: Rather than fighting for a slice of traditional banking rails that were never built with North Africa in mind, a handful of startups are building on top of borderless, 24/7 digital money and designing the user experience around local realities from day one.

item.title: Nigeria’s digital lenders stay cautious as CBN cuts benchmark rate
item.description: Digital lenders in Nigeria may begin cautiously lowering borrowing costs after the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) cut the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) to 26.5% from 27% on Tuesday, signalling a potential easing of the country’s prolonged high-interest-rate environment.

item.title: Samsung Galaxy Unpacked 2026: What’s different from 2025
item.description: The global smartphone industry is now driven by AI built directly into your device. For Samsung Electronics, the main stage for showing this vision is the Galaxy Unpacked event series.

item.title: Only 20 Nigerian banks meet new capital requirements as March deadline nears
item.description: Only 20 of Nigeria’s 33 deposit money banks have met the Central Bank of Nigeria’s (CBN) new minimum capital requirements less than a month before the March 31, 2026, deadline.
